objective: Compare multipath and single-path transport arms by useful application work delivered before deadlines, cost and energy per on-time useful MiB, deadline misses, redundancy overhead, shared-resource safety and companion-flow retention.

paradigm.primary: Optimize deadline-qualified useful application work rather than raw packet throughput.

rfc_6356_compatibility.purpose: Retain the established MPTCP compatibility/fairness reference as a separate experimental track.

num_utility_exploration.purpose: Compare utility-oriented allocations, including NUM-inspired controllers, without silently treating the RFC best-path principle as the only possible research objective.

scenario_definitions.name: small-deadline-control-mixed-with-bulk
scenario_definitions.purpose: Measure short control tasks competing with a long bulk transfer.

scenario_definitions.name: heterogeneous-size-deadline-value
scenario_definitions.purpose: Vary task size, deadline and application value weights.

scenario_definitions.name: expensive-cellular-cheap-wifi-feasible
scenario_definitions.purpose: Compare cost-aware path choice when both paths can meet deadline.

scenario_definitions.name: cheap-path-misses-deadline
scenario_definitions.purpose: Test whether a more expensive path is justified by timely task value.

scenario_definitions.name: deadline-infeasible-on-all-paths
scenario_definitions.purpose: Avoid spending scarce capacity on hopeless retransmission after a task deadline is infeasible.

scenario_definitions.name: partial-useful-streaming-chunks
scenario_definitions.purpose: Credit on-time chunks without granting value to late chunks.

scenario_definitions.name: high-throughput-high-tail-delay-vs-lower-latency
scenario_definitions.purpose: Compare high-throughput high-jitter paths with lower-throughput low-tail-delay alternatives.

scenario_definitions.name: redundancy-under-shared-backhaul
scenario_definitions.purpose: Measure deadline reliability gains and duplicate-byte cost under a shared bottleneck.

scenario_definitions.name: multipath-throughput-vs-companion-starvation
scenario_definitions.purpose: Reject apparent gains that materially reduce a competing TCP/QUIC flow's service.

scenario_definitions.name: congestion-burst-and-controller-recovery
scenario_definitions.purpose: Measure recovery and regret after a congestion or loss burst.

scenario_definitions.name: stale-or-missing-task-metadata
scenario_definitions.purpose: Ensure missing/stale task metadata produces inconclusive or unsupported outcomes.

scenario_definitions.name: untrusted-controller-or-binary-identity
scenario_definitions.purpose: Reject unknown or unpinned external implementations from qualification.

scenario_definitions.name: paired-task-or-environment-mismatch
scenario_definitions.purpose: Reject treatment/control pairs with different task sets, seeds or environment digests.

scenario_definitions.name: NUM-vs-RFC-objective-tradeoff
scenario_definitions.purpose: Compare RFC 6356-compatible behavior against a NUM-oriented research controller while retaining fairness, resource and companion-flow gates.

explicit_non_claims: The evaluator does not implement N-MPTCP, DaMPS, CaDaMPS, DART, MPTCP, QUIC or any congestion controller.
The evaluator does not schedule packets or actuate a route, qdisc or radio.
Application value units are supplied by a frozen workload oracle; the network does not infer human value.
Late useful bytes are reported but do not count as on-time useful work.
A paired-trial pass is not programme-level statistical qualification.
The NUM-oriented track is experimental and does not silently replace RFC 6356 compatibility evaluation.
Paper-reported DaMPS/CaDaMPS or N-MPTCP percentages are not accepted as directly comparable results without matching workload and implementation identities.
No claim of beating Linux MPTCP, Multipath QUIC, DaMPS, CaDaMPS or DART is made without exact pinned measured comparisons.
No namespace, hardware or field measurement is claimed by the pure evaluator.
